text:
sam: quick idea — implement a lightweight probabilistic hotset sampler + compact-on-write for large model shards to reduce fragmentation and avoid full-evict churn
carla: short version: track hot byte ranges inside a shard and prefer to allocate new writes into hot holes?
marta: can you sketch how sampler works and how it hooks into allocator?
sam: yeah. sampler is a tiny per-range saturating counter (configurable range: 4KB/64KB). we increment on each access with probabilistic sampling for very hot flows. background aggregator computes hotset sketches per-tenant. when compaction decision triggers for a shard we pick one of: 1) in-place compact if reserve staging available, or 2) compact-on-write: the next write to a cold range synchronously relocates nearby hot ranges and remaps their entries, or 3) async compaction scheduled if sync budget exceeded.
jiro: compact-on-write might add latency to first write path — how do we bound that?
sam: two levers: synchronous budget cap (max_work_ms) and deferred write path. default budget < 2ms; if exceeded we enqueue to worker pool and let the write proceed with a slower fallback policy. we also batch small compactions to amortize overhead.
carla: allocator integration: how are remaps done without exposing stale pointers for KV cache or pinned refs?
marta: allocator exposes an atomic remap API: allocate into staging, write new map entry, publish via epoch bump, then free old pages after epoch drains. two-phase publish + idempotent free. similar semantics to existing offload handoff.
jiro: tenant fairness — compaction is IO/GPU heavy. a noisy tenant could hog compaction workers and bandwidth.
sam: planner will track per-tenant compaction credits derived from reserved throughput; credits replenish over time. once credits depleted, compactions are queued and backpressured. we also emit chargeback metrics so teams can see compaction cost.
carla: staging / storage overhead? this seems to need extra headroom.
sam: yes; proposal is a small ephemeral staging pool per-node (default 3% of node memory) that compaction borrows from. pool is tagged with eviction priority and can be reclaimed under pressure. we prefer reusing existing host-staging/pinned pools when safe, but tagged isolation helps noisy neighbor protection.
marta: eviction interplay: if compaction moves hot pages into staging and eviction runs, we might shuffle same pages multiple times.
sam: sampler ties into eviction scoring — hot-range weight reduces eviction score for compacted pages. compaction aims to cluster hot pages to increase locality, lowering chance of immediate re-eviction.
jiro: failure scenarios? compaction worker crash mid-remap could corrupt serving map.
sam: from serving plane view, remap is atomic. compactor does: copy -> publish new mapping -> schedule old free after epoch. if worker dies before publish, no change; if dies after publish but before free, old memory reclaimed on recovery. all steps are idempotent; we have retry logic and a compaction journal for visibility. example logs: 
[compactor] start tenant=acme shard=0x7fa3 budget_ms=2
[compactor] copied 128KB -> staging @node3
[compactor] publish remap epoch=42
[compactor] free old 128KB
carla: telemetry we should expose: compaction_count, avg_compaction_ms, bytes_relocated, cold_write_p95, tenant_compaction_credits_used, compactor_queue_length.
marta: security/compliance: ensure compaction never crosses tenant boundary and respects KMS/HSM and network isolation. compaction operates within tenant's reachable host/gpu set only.
jiro: rollout plan?
sam: opt-in runtime flag per-tenant. phase 0: sampler-only telemetry for two weeks (no compaction) to validate patterns; phase 1: enable compact-on-write for low-traffic tenants and strict budget; phase 2: expand to more tenants with adaptive crediting after a month. keep a kill-switch per-node and per-tenant.
carla: +1 telemetry-first. PoC? I can pair tomorrow.
marta: I'll review allocator remap API and epoch drain semantics.
jiro: infra-bot, create tracker.
infra-bot: created issue RUNTIME-1248: "probabilistic hotset sampler + compact-on-write PoC" and linked this thread. :robot_face: 
sam: thanks — i'll post a prototype patch and perf harness link later today. :thumbsup:
